root_cause.text: The DACL rewrite helpers for chmod/chown (replace_sids_and_copy_aces and set_chmod_dacl) processed ACEs based on the server-supplied num_aces header field without validating that each ACE structure actually fits within the DACL buffer, enabling a malicious server to cause out-of-bounds memory access by returning a truncated DACL with a valid header but insufficient ACE data.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states: "The original fix only checked that the struct smb_acl header fits before reading dacl_ptr->size or dacl_ptr->num_aces. That avoids the immediate header-field OOB read, but the rewrite helpers still walk ACEs based on pdacl->num_aces with no structural validation of the incoming DACL body." The patch adds validate_dacl() which validates each ACE’s size and bounds, and then uses it in both parse_dacl() (read-side) and in build_sec_desc()/id_mode_to_cifs_acl() (write-side) before the rewrite helpers are called.

candidates.rationale: Loop iterates based on server-supplied num_aces without per-ACE bounds validation, allowing out-of-bounds access if num_aces exceeds actual buffer space.
Directly computes pointer into DACL buffer using acl_size, which may be corrupted by previous iterations or insufficiently validated, leading to out-of-bounds read/write.
Trusts the server-supplied ACE size field, which can be set to arbitrary large value, causing subsequent pointer calculations to exceed buffer bounds.
Assumes each ACE has fixed size (sizeof(struct smb_ace)), ignoring variable-length SIDs; this can underestimate required memory and cause buffer overflow when processing aces.
This validation check uses a fixed ACE size denominator, failing to account for variable-length SIDs; therefore it does not prevent out-of-bounds access when ACEs have extra sub-authorities.

    parse_dcal() validate num_aces to allocate ace array.
    
    f (num_aces > ULONG_MAX / sizeof(struct smb_ace *))
    
    It is an incorrect validation that we can create an array of size ULONG_MAX.

bic_trace_step.reason: The commit replaces the incorrect validation 'if (num_aces > ULONG_MAX / sizeof(struct smb_ace *))' with a proper check that uses the ACL size to bound num_aces: 'if (num_aces > (le16_to_cpu(pdacl->size) - sizeof(struct smb_acl)) / (offsetof(struct smb_ace, sid) + offsetof(struct smb_sid, sub_auth) + sizeof(__le16)))'. This ensures the number of ACEs does not exceed what fits in the buffer, preventing the out-of-bounds access described in the root cause. Additionally, an ACL header size validation is added. Both changes constitute the fix.
